notes: an expression with no variable and no call answers three empty lists
each variable is one reference, in source order
a property chain is one reference whose path runs from the root variable
every occurrence is listed; a caller that wants a set dedupes
a literal integer index is an integer segment
a literal string key is a string segment, the same as a property
a computed key is the dynamic segment; the path continues past it, and the key's own reads follow the chain
a literal key that is neither a string nor an integer is the dynamic segment too
both operands of a membership test are read
reads inside list and object literals are listed; a chain rooted at a literal reads no variable
the operands of and and or are listed in source order
a call lists its name and arity; its argument is a reference
a qualified name is reported as written, dots included
a call nested in another call's arguments is listed, the outer call first
calls in sibling arguments are listed left to right after the outer call
a chain rooted at a call's result reads no variable: the argument is the only reference
the location an assignment writes is not a read; its value's reads are
each statement's store is listed in source order
literal bracket keys in a location are string and integer segments
a computed key in a location is the dynamic segment, and the key itself is a read

source: if overdue { standing = 'blocked' } else { notices[day] = len(holds) }
notes: stores inside both branches of an if are listed, with the condition's and the branches' reads and calls

source: count = 0; while count < len(holds) { count = count + 1 }
notes: a while loop's condition and body are read once each, in source order
an instruction list carries no positions: every position is null
a store whose segment is not a string or integer literal stores to the dynamic segment, and that segment's reads are listed
the retired and opcode still reads both operands
